Hey @infinitydon 

In general all the binaries can be launched asynchronously. If something has a cross dependency on another it will go into a 'connect' loop in the background until the other part comes online; eg you can start the MME before the HSS.

@infinitydon 

As @kbarlee mentioned earlier, you can run any NFs regardless of the startup sequence. However, configuration reloading is currently not supported. So, if you change the configuration, you need to restart the NF.

Let me know if you have any further questions.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

Thanks @kbarlee and @acetcom.

As per my last point:

Is it possible for the SMF to start without specifying the UPF address? A sample scenario for this will be in a edge case where SMF is running in a central cloud and UPF runs in edge locations, so that SMF PFCP will start in server-mode and the UPF can connect to the SMF as they are created without re-configuring/restarting the SMF?

In theory I think so? I normally have the SMF list IPs of the UPFs (so that it can do logical selection, slice etc) meaning the SMF initiates the PFCP connections ; and the UPF configs don't list SMF IPs.

But I guess it can be done the other way round?

@infinitydon 

You can do it by changing the configuration as below.

- smf.conf
```diff
$ diff --git a/configs/open5gs/smf.yaml.in b/configs/open5gs/smf.yaml.in
index 728b0835..e5db5eab 100644
--- a/configs/open5gs/smf.yaml.in
+++ b/configs/open5gs/smf.yaml.in
@@ -426,8 +426,6 @@ nrf:
 #        nr_cell_id: [123456789, 9413]
 #
 upf:
-    pfcp:
-      - addr: 127.0.0.7
 
 #
 # parameter:
```

- upf.conf
```diff
$ diff --git a/configs/open5gs/upf.yaml.in b/configs/open5gs/upf.yaml.in
index b9562337..f30d6b92 100644
--- a/configs/open5gs/upf.yaml.in
+++ b/configs/open5gs/upf.yaml.in
@@ -156,6 +156,8 @@ upf:
 #      addr: 127.0.0.3
 #
You can do it by changing the settings as below.
 smf:
+    pfcp:
+      addr: 127.0.0.4
 
 #
 # parameter:

```

Good luck with you!
Sukchan

@infinitydon 

I found the exact reason for the above error. There is no need to provide conf file or PCAP.

It does not occur when there is an UPF PFCP IP address in the smf.yaml as the default configuration file. It only happens when there is SMF PFCP IP address in the upf.yaml as you do.

I'll let you know when I fix it.

Thank you for raising this issue.
Sukchan

@infinitydon and @kbarlee 

Now, the above bug is fixed in the main branch.

For your reference, the configuration usage has changed. PFCP node rr=0 is removed as shown below.
```
sgwc:
  pfcp
    rr: 0 <-- Removed
```

Now, I introduced a new configuration method for SMF/SGW-C

```
parameter:
   no_pfcp_rr_select: true
```

By default, PFCP round robin selection is allowed. The above parameters prohibit selecting PFCP in a round robin manner.

Let me know if you have any questions about this!

Thank you so much!
Sukchan

Hey @acetcom  

If you check my original commit https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/pull/560/commits/e9d084dd949f627a56ba515b945b7b175ae18d4d with the `rr: 0` feature, there is a description explaining what it did. 

Basically the following scenario (consider either `sgwc.yaml` or `smf.yaml`) :

```
    pfcp:

      - addr: 127.0.1.4  # userplaneserver1 for IMS (centralised)
        apn: ims

      - addr: 127.0.2.4  # userplaneserver2 for TAC 1 region
        tac: 1

      - addr: 127.0.3.4  # userplaneserver3 for TAC 2 region
        tac: 2

      - addr: 127.0.4.4  # userplaneserver4 at cell site
        e_cell_id: 123
        nr_cell_id: 321
        rr: 0            # do not allow this userplaneserver to be selected when performing full list RR, 
                         #  as there is no S1U/N3 VPN to other eNB/gNBs

      - addr: 127.0.5.4  # userplaneserver5 at cell site
        e_cell_id: 456
        nr_cell_id: 654
        rr: 0            # do not allow this userplaneserver to be selected when performing full list RR, 
                         #  as there is no S1U/N3 VPN to other eNB/gNBs

      - addr: 127.0.6.4  # userplaneserver6 for edge compute use case 1/2
        apn: [mec1, mec2]    
        rr: 0            # do not allow this userplaneserver to be selected when performing full list RR, 
                         #  no internet connectivity (only edge servers for data crunch)

      - addr: 127.0.7.4  # userplaneserver7 for edge compute use case 1/2
        apn: [mec1, mec2]
        rr: 0            # do not allow this userplaneserver to be selected when performing full list RR, 
                         #  no internet connectivity (only edge servers for data crunch)

      - addr: 127.0.8.4  # userplaneserver8 at cell site, also used for edge compute use case 3
        e_cell_id: 789
        nr_cell_id: 897
        apn: mec3
```

Then we consider a series of UE logical tests, in order of selection priority, and will assign the UE to the respective SGWu/UPF if the node is PFCP associated. (Skip to next option if not):

### APN/DNN selection (top priority, if there is a match here dont run other tests; etc down list)
`ims` goes to `127.0.1.4`
UE#1 `mec1`  goes to `127.0.6.4`
UE#2 `mec1`  goes to `127.0.7.4`
UE#3 `mec1`  goes to `127.0.6.4` ..etc as we RR inside each of these 
`mec2`  goes to `127.0.6.4` / `127.0.7.4`
`mec3`  goes to `127.0.8.4` only

### e_cell_ID selection
`e_cell_id = 123` goes to `127.0.4.4`
`e_cell_id = 456` goes to `127.0.5.4`
`e_cell_id = 789` goes to `127.0.8.4` 

### nr_cell_ID selection
`nr_cell_id= 321` goes to `127.0.4.4`
`nr_cell_id= 654` goes to `127.0.5.4`
`nr_cell_id= 897` goes to `127.0.8.4` 

### tac selection
`tac= 1` goes to `127.0.2.4`
`tac= 2` goes to `127.0.3.4`

### No match on anything we are testing for // OR the node selected was not PFCP associated
... now we do round robin between remaining PFCP associated nodes that have `rr: 1` (default option)
* UE#1 goes to `127.0.1.4`
* UE#2 goes to `127.0.2.4`
* UE#3 goes to `127.0.3.4`
* UE#4 goes to `127.0.8.4`
* UE#5 goes to `127.0.1.4` and repeats.

If any of these SGWu/UPFs are not associated they will be skipped in the RR list. If all else fails, something must be chosen. Therefore the default was to use the first item in the list. That's the message that was getting printed out above.
```
[sgwc / smf] ERROR: No UPFs are PFCP associated that are suited to RR

return ogs_list_first(&ogs_pfcp_self()->peer_list);

[sgwc / smf] DEBUG: UE using UPF on IP[127.0.1.4]
```

____

With the change made in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/commit/fc27f7499b29ae2d191272312f3d89f88d4bdbf6 this logical flow can no longer be supported, as RR is either enabled or disabled for the entire list. You cannot make RR skip some entries that are no good for RR, such as for SGWu/UPFs installed at edge compute sites for `mec1` `mec2` etc that have no internet access, or to skip nodes that have no VPN connection to the serving eNB/gNB.

____

As I mentioned in above comment, this situation only arises as the SGWu/UPF list in @infinitydon 's `sgwc.yaml` and `smf.yaml` dont contain any nodes. Therefore this functionality can be retained by rolling back and instead adding an option to ignore all selection logic in the situation the pfcp lists are emtpy. 

A question I have, however, is why this situation would occur. The SGWc/SMF should know the SGWu/UPF that are connecting in to it, and therefore there should always be some defined in this list. If running blind, like here, then some method of accessing PFCP associated nodes that are _undefined_ needs to be incorporated.

Cheers
Kenny

Hi @kbarlee 

```
A question I have, however, is why this situation would occur. The SGWc/SMF should know the SGWu/UPF that are connecting in to it, and therefore there should always be some defined in this list. If running blind, like here, then some method of accessing PFCP associated nodes that are undefined needs to be incorporated.
```

I don't think that all UPF nodes need to be defined in the SMF configuration. Standard allow it to be used with @infinitydon method.

In @infinitydon  configuration, SMF configuration has no UPF node information. In that case there is no way to set rr:0 to a specific PFCP node.

So, to reduce user's misunderstanding, I removed rr:0 in the smf configuration

Cheers!
Sukchan
